text: The Patriots bid farewell to one of their greatest defensive players this week as Stephon Gilmore, the 2019 NFL Defensive Player of the Year and two-time All-Pro cornerback, retired as a member of New England after signing a one-day contract on Friday—a fitting send-off for a franchise legend who helped anchor some of the team's most dominant defensive efforts. On the injury front, the news is mixed heading into Sunday's Week 2 home opener against the Steelers: running back TreVeyon Henderson, who missed last week's game with an ankle injury, declared himself "ready to go" Thursday and is expected to return, but the Patriots could be without starting cornerback Carlton Davis III, who is officially questionable for the matchup. Beyond the roster, the Patriots organization has been in the headlines for other reasons, with owner Robert Kraft making headlines for removing rapper Macklemore as an opening act for Ed Sheeran's upcoming shows at Gillette Stadium, citing "a history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community." Meanwhile, the club continues its international expansion efforts, with Pro Football Hall of Famer Adam Vinatieri set to attempt a Guinness World Record kick at Jungfraujoch in the Swiss Alps as part of the promotion for New England's upcoming game in Munich.
